policy.note: Permissive licences whose only obligation is attribution, which this project satisfies by shipping the SBOM. Everything else is reviewed individually below.

reviewed.note: The publisher declares no licence the SBOM tool could resolve. An unlicensed component is not permissively licensed — it is a component with no grant at all — so this is an unanswered obligation rather than a formatting problem.
Weak copyleft at file level. The component is consumed unmodified as a dependency, so the obligation is to publish changes to its own files and there are none.

Disjunctive with a copyleft alternative. This project takes the BSD-3-Clause option, which is the whole point of recording the choice: leaving it implicit would make the dependency tree look like it contains GPL-2.0 code under obligation.
A content licence on a data package rather than a code licence. Attribution is the only obligation and the package is redistributed unmodified.
The publisher declares the same permissive licence twice, which the SBOM tool preserves as two entries. No obligation beyond attribution; recorded verbatim so the duplication stays visible.
Disjunctive: this project takes the MIT option. Both alternatives are permissive; the choice is recorded rather than left implicit.

Permissive, attribution only. No copyleft obligation and no restriction on commercial use or distribution.

notPublished.reason: The image is built by whoever deploys it, from the Dockerfile in this repository, and is never pushed to a registry, so there is no published digest for a consumer to compare against.

The APK is produced by the CI android job to prove the native channel compiles and links, and is retained as a workflow artifact rather than released, so it has no published digest and no signing identity.
